evidence: at least twelve vulnerable cases … with EXPECTED.md as the manifest delivered as twelve fixtures V-001..V-012 across eleven languages (TypeScript, Java, Go, Python, C#, JavaScript, Ruby, YAML, HCL, Kotlin, Apex), one bug class per file, each row carrying filename, language, bug class, expected severity, expected CWE, owning lens and topic, and the specific severity row or checklist item that should fire

one bug class per major lens, each with the expected severity and CWE recorded in the manifest — coverage spans six owning lenses (web-and-api x4, crypto-and-key-management x3, llm-and-ai, cicd-and-supply-chain, cloud-and-iac, mobile-app-security, salesforce-platform) and each fixture's sweep run is recorded with its exit status; 11 of 12 are found by their owning lens's own machinery and the one that is not is recorded as known gap 1 rather than tuned

no working payloads, no real or realistic-looking credentials … a README warning explaining why the directory exists … written from scratch, never reduced from real code — README states each rule with the reason; every fixture is inert (no main, no listener, no provider block, no deployable metadata, unresolvable imports) and every credential-shaped literal is structurally invalid, with the cost of that rule recorded honestly as known gap 3

The design says "fixtures/ excluded from code scanning". A .gitattributes cannot express that: it reaches GitHub Linguist, not CodeQL, Semgrep, Snyk or Dependabot, each of which reads its own configuration. Implemented as `fixtures/** linguist-vendored` (keeps the corpus out of language stats, rendered diffs and code search) with the residual stated in the same words in both .gitattributes and fixtures/README.md, so the two cannot drift and nobody reads the attribute as a scanner exclusion it is not
